selected_sources.population: FOS: 2473 predominantly white adults >=25, prior antidiabetic treatment or FPG >=126 excluded; NHANES 2001-2004: 3270 adults >=25, self-reported diagnosed diabetes or FPG >=126 excluded, A1c available. NHANES lacks OGTT. These are not the Mexico equal-cell design.
selected_sources.measurement: DCCT-standardized HPLC HbA1c percent; hexokinase plasma fasting glucose mg/dL. Plasma-to-serum measurement transport is unresolved.
selected_sources.weighting: NHANES analyses incorporate complex design and sampling weights; FOS is a community cohort. Their estimators are not the task's equal-cell WLS.

selected_sources.population: Selected general Finnish population Health 2011 subset n=653, ages 30-64; Maamu Russian/Somali/Kurdish groups are comparative context. Excludes diabetes identified from registers, medication, self-report, HbA1c >=6.5%, or fasting glucose >=7.0 mmol/L; complete variables and fast 4-17 hours. These restrictions differ materially from HC.
selected_sources.measurement: BMI kg/m^2 from standardized standing height/weight; immunoturbidimetric HbA1c percent; Finnish general-population glucose measured in serum mmol/L, Maamu glucose in fluoride-citrate plasma.
selected_sources.weighting_and_adjustment: Stratified sampling, finite population correction and inverse-probability nonresponse/sampling weights. Age is 30-44 versus 45-64. Supplement S1/S2 list age + sex + BMI. Methods additionally state glucose analyses adjusted for fasting time; the displayed S1 block lacks a fasting-time coefficient, so its exact source replay remains unavailable. Main Table 1 means/CIs are predictive margins, not raw individual moments.

selected_sources.population: Kerman, Iran proportional-cluster household study ages 18-75; total n=604. FBS<=126 subgroup n=525 includes 30 reporting diabetes, unlike HC's diagnosis exclusion. One fasting glucose measurement; a precise fasting-duration distribution is not available in the inspected methods.
selected_sources.measurement: FBS mg/dL by enzyme method, HbA1c percent using Biosystem kit. Analysis reports Pearson correlation; no survey weighting correction is described for it.

uses.use: True reported individual SD context only. HC glucose mean 94 and conditional SD 10 are deliberate selected-population assumptions, not an attempted exact reconstruction. HbA1c SD 0.73 is marginal and is not substituted as a residual SD. BMI mean/SD declined for direct transport in favor of the larger diagnosis-excluded NHANES mean and explicit shape/dispersion assumptions.

Retain evidence of imperfect positive association, but decline reported Table 2 raw slopes because the units/scaling are inconsistent with Table 1 SDs and reported r under ordinary raw OLS. Deterministic r*SD(H)/SD(G)=0.013540322580645161, reverse=3.9068493150684938; these differ from 0.13 and 0.38. Do not silently correct the publication or treat the derived marginal slope as an adjusted slope. Choose conditional H-on-G slope 0.01 explicitly as A_JOINT. Own-law marginal r=0.4127835441198015 is not a source replay or a match to 0.23; population/selection/design differences and unknown dependence prevent attribution of that discrepancy.

selected_sources.population: Taiwan Biobank, 4748 adults aged 30-70 without previous diabetes diagnosis; not all fasting; latent diabetes and HbA1c >=6.5 remain possible. A female-count discrepancy exists between methods and results.
selected_sources.use: Qualitative evidence that no previous diagnosis does not justify imposing HbA1c<6.5. No numerical parameter adopted because fasting and age selection do not match HC and full BMI/glucose adjustment is absent. Its much higher reported extreme HbA1c is outside this developmental model's support; extreme-tail fidelity is expressly unresolved. Its discussion of PMC2551641 is secondary citation, not independent replication.

overlap_and_versions: XML/text/JSON extractions of one paper are one evidence item. Finnish Tables S1/S2 and R2 share participants; their estimates are statistically dependent. FOS and NHANES are distinct cohorts within one publication. No participant overlap is established among the US, Finland, Kerman and Taiwan studies, but absence of documented overlap is not proof of independence. Selected table extraction and XML report take precedence over differing rounded narrative summaries; no effect estimates were precision-pooled.

assumptions.statement: The task fixes variables, units, 3000 rows, eight cells of 375 and all three analysis IDs. It supplies no desired coefficient/sign or target statistics.
Uniform age within each prescribed band, independently sampled; equal sex and band masses. No national population age/sex distribution is implied.

The law is conditional on the complete stated eligibility context. Unrepresented diagnosis, fasting-duration and documentation features are assumed satisfied, with pregnancy/lactation handling as specified. Medication/anemia are not assumed absent; their specific effects and selection probabilities are unidentified.

Selected US and Finnish source point associations are transferred to Mexico with no validated population, assay, serum/plasma or fasting-duration correction. Finland's HbA1c restriction, diabetes medication exclusion, age adjustment and source weights are not silently adopted as HC restrictions. Transfer is a scenario, not source reproduction.

Finnish 30-44 and 45-64 bins are replaced by their arithmetic midpoints 37 and 54.5, giving 17.5 years. The binary glucose contrast divided by this gap is extended linearly to ages 25-79. Actual source mean ages and transport of this linear shape are unknown.

BMI is independent of age/female; glucose has linear conditional mean; HbA1c conditional glucose slope is 0.01 percentage points per mg/dL; effects are constant and innovations independent. The derived direct BMI slope is 0.0125-0.01*0.432=0.00818. Thus changing the unidentified conditional glucose slope changes Q3 and the Q2/Q3 difference even if the reduced BMI slope remains 0.0125. No conditional slope was recovered from source marginal r.

BMI SD 5.5, glucose conditional SD 10, HbA1c conditional residual SD 0.32, glucose center 94 and HbA1c center 5.45 are explicit author choices in the context of observed source scales. No SE-to-SD or predictive-margin-CI-to-SD conversion was used. The own-law marginal HbA1c SD is larger than 0.32 because covariates explain variation.

Scaled beta BMI support (14,55), glucose support (45,126) and symmetric Beta(4,4) HbA1c residuals are chosen finite-support shapes, not empirically established bounds or clinical rules. They ensure positive finite outputs and avoid artificial mass at an eligibility clamp. Extreme tails, heteroscedasticity and subgroup-tail differences remain unmodeled.
